questions.question_english: A noun object can be placed either before or after the adverbial particle. questions.question_english: Two-word separable phrasal verbs permit object insertion, whereas three-word phrasal verbs are always inseparable. Syntactically, two-word separable phrasal verbs allow noun phrase objects to intervene between the verb and particle. In contrast, three-word phrasal-prepositional verbs consist of a verb, an adverbial particle, and a preposition. Because the third element is a functional preposition heading a prepositional phrase, these three-word units are strictly inseparable, requiring all nominal complements to follow the trailing preposition directly without exception.
